clue.text: With organised group one can stop it!

parts.note: a pack is a band of people or animals acting together
the Roman numeral for one is I
a tin is a can, as of beans

explanation.surface: A rallying cry: an organised group could put a stop to some nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial command to quit or desist, so it serves as an exclamation meaning cease that.

clue.text: All the players' stakes in game

definitions.meaning: the pot or kitty of money staked by every player in a gambling round
a cue game like snooker or billiards, played on a table with pockets

explanation.definitionFit: A pool is both a combined fund of bets and a billiards-type table game.

clue.text: Conservative with axe to grind

parts.note: to axe or chop with a blade is to hew

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who has a personal grievance to pursue.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind food between the teeth is to masticate it, the same action.

clue.text: Increase in prices of fashionable property upset no-one

parts.note: in means trendy or in vogue
a flat is an apartment, a piece of property

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so this piece reads from the bottom up

parts.note: split as NO plus ONE, with one becoming the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A complaint that the cost of trendy homes has gone up, and nobody is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NOI (NO plus I) to give ION. 'no-one' pretends to mean nobody but is read as two words, with one giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use the term for a general rise in the cost of goods over time.

clue.text: Cobbled street in a Utrillo sketch

indicators.note: cobbled means roughly put together, so these letters are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the surname of the painter, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cobbled Paris street features in a drawing by Maurice Utrillo, the Montmartre painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobbled' looks like a description of the street, but it is the anagram signal on ST + IN + A + UTRILLO. Utrillo was a French painter famous for Montmartre street scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a drawing or picture, as one might find in a book.

clue.text: Climber reading, say, information on map first

indicators.note: first says the map information comes before the other piece in the answer

parts.note: a scale is the ratio printed on a map showing distances
reading is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it

explanation.surface: A mountaineer studying the map details before setting out.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'reading, say' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: One who climbs, such as a mountaineer, scales peaks, so is a scaler.

clue.text: Change letter in "rub", making "rib"

indicators.note: says one letter of the word for rub is swapped for another

parts.note: to chafe is to rub, as tight shoes do

explanation.surface: A word-game instruction to alter one letter so that one word becomes another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change letter in' swaps the E at the end of CHAFE for an F.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to tease them, and banter or teasing is also called chaff.

clue.text: Party members in Tribune also rejecting "new", perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps means the remaining letters are only one possible arrangement, to be reworked
rejecting says a letter is thrown out of the word Tribune

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Readers of Tribune, the left-wing weekly, are turning against New Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes N out of TRIBUNE, and 'perhaps' scrambles TRIBUE plus ALSO. Tribune is a British left-wing magazine, and New Labour was Tony Blair's rebranding of the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters belonging to the Labour Party in Britain are called by this name.

clue.text: Measure of spin showing Tory slant

parts.note: the Tories are the political right
an angle is a slant or point of view on a story

explanation.surface: A remark about political spin doctors putting a Tory slant on the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter turn of rotation is ninety degrees, so it is a unit of turning.

clue.text: Rock layers about to collapse

parts.note: over means about or concerning, as in a row over money
to fold is to collapse, as a business folds

explanation.surface: Strata of rock are on the point of falling in.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology this term names a fold of strata turned past the vertical, so the layers are inverted.

clue.text: Blimp as CO, perhaps, has to talk back

parts.note: CO, carbon monoxide, is an example of a gas

indicators.note: back means the word for talk is read in the other direction

parts.note: gab is chatter or talk

explanation.surface: A Colonel Blimp figure who, as commanding officer, has to answer back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GAB into BAG. CO looks like commanding officer, which suits Colonel Blimp, the pompous cartoon officer, but it is the chemical formula.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, essentially a large envelope filled with lighter-than-air vapour.

clue.text: Recollected action in field with loss of one private

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means gathered up again in a new order
with loss of says a letter is removed from the gathered words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A soldier remembers combat on the battlefield, having lost a comrade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with loss of' takes one I out of ACTION IN FIELD, and 'Recollected' rearranges the rest. 'private' looks like a soldier's rank but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something private is secret, not to be shared outside a trusted circle.

clue.text: What's picked to produce a crush?

definitions.text: What's picked to produce a crush?

parts.words: What's picked to produce a crush?
parts.note: a crush can be a fruit drink made by squashing fruit, or an infatuation; the item picked is a fruit whose name suggests ardent love

explanation.definitionFit: This tropical fruit is gathered and squeezed for juice, and its name evokes intense love, which a crush is.

clue.text: Awkward, unlike today's child

parts.note: un- is the prefix of negation, meaning not or unlike
in the rhyme, Tuesday's child is full of grace, and the puzzle appeared on a Tuesday

explanation.surface: A complaint that children nowadays are clumsy, quite unlike the old rhyme says.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face, Tuesday's child is full of grace' supplies the key: today is Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, lacking elegance of movement, is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Isle of Man doing all in order

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: put in order means the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man getting everything sorted out properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isle of Man' looks like one name, but Isle is the definition and Man gives HE; 'in order' rearranges DOING ALL. Heligoland is a small German island in the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an island off the German coast in the North Sea.

clue.text: I have turned in unsuspecting moles

indicators.note: turned in says the contraction sitting inside the word for unsuspecting is flipped round where it stands

parts.note: naive means innocent and unsuspecting
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone innocent has had their skin blemishes reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have' contracts to I've; 'turned in' flips those letters where they sit at the end of NAIVE, making EVI.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi is the plural of naevus, a birthmark or skin mole.

clue.text: Thought pound should be discounted for meal

indicators.note: discounted means left out of the reckoning, so a letter is removed

parts.note: reflection is careful thought
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A shopper reckons a pound should be knocked off the price of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be discounted' removes L from REFLECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Refection is an old word for refreshment, especially a light repast.

clue.text: Bones shrank, say, leading to shortness of backbone

indicators.note: leading to says this piece comes in front of the other
say means the word for shrank is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: shrank in fear means cowered
dice are traditionally called bones, being once made of bone

explanation.surface: Bones shrinking as one ages leads to a weakened spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes COWARD from COWERED, the past tense of cower. Dice are called bones from the old material they were carved from.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of backbone means lack of courage, which is timidity.

clue.text: Caught again before end of match?

definitions.text: Caught again before end of match?

parts.words: Caught again before end of match?
parts.note: caught refers to fire catching once more, as a flame might relight before a matchstick burns out, while suggesting a cricket catch

explanation.definitionFit: A fire that has caught again has been set alight once more.

clue.text: American cheese with end of loaf

parts.note: the heel is the crust at the end of a loaf

explanation.surface: Ordering American cheese with the crust of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'big cheese' is an important person; Americans also say 'big wheel'.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a big shot or important person is called this, like a big cheese.

clue.text: Race, scoot, scurry, run, finally scramble

indicators.note: scramble means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of run

explanation.surface: A list of hurried movements in a race over rough terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N from run, and 'scramble' rearranges it with SCOOT and SCURRY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-distance running event over open country rather than a track.

clue.text: Fragment cast, dropping in river

indicators.note: dropping in means a letter is put into the word for cast

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: An angler's cast loses something in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny piece or scrap is a fragment of something larger.

clue.text: Like flexible rod twisted about one

indicators.note: about means the word for twisted goes round the other piece

parts.note: wry means twisted or contorted
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A bendy rod bent round on itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean, tough and pliable like a length of metal strand describes this.

clue.text: Come to watch

definitions.meaning: to regain consciousness or rouse from sleep
a vigil kept over a dead body before burial

explanation.definitionFit: To rouse from sleep and a vigil beside a corpse share this one word.

clue.text: Transport provided back to port

indicators.note: back means the word for provided is read the other way round

parts.note: if means provided that
Acre is a historic port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: Goods carried, on condition they return to the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IF into FI. Acre is an old Mediterranean port.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre is a small horse-drawn hackney carriage, a mode of conveyance.

clue.text: Half-hearted encouragement at home given a female out East

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two letters at the heart of the word is lost

parts.note: a fillip is a boost or encouragement
in means at home

explanation.surface: A woman abroad in the Far East gets only lukewarm support at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' removes one of the two central Ls of FILLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman from the Philippines, a country in the Far East, is called this.

clue.text: Youth takes girl to be uppity

parts.note: a lad is a youth
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young man thinks his girlfriend is getting above herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious and snobbish in manner, putting on airs, is what both words describe.

clue.text: Helium put back into possibly deadly compound

indicators.note: into means the turned piece goes inside the jumbled letters
possibly means the letters of deadly are rearranged
put back means the symbol is reversed

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: Helium being returned into a lethal chemical mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deadly' looks like a description of the compound, but 'possibly' makes it anagram fodder; the reversed helium symbol sits inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a class of organic chemical, such as formaldehyde.
